# Trippo

> Trippo is a Hungarian mileage log (útnyilvántartás) and travel order (kiküldetési rendelvény) app for iPhone. It records trips by itself with GPS, and at month end it makes the PDF and Excel for the accountant, with every field the Hungarian tax authority (NAV) requires. It is for sole traders (egyéni vállalkozó), Kft. owners, employees who drive their own car for work, and company cars.

Key facts:
- Platform: iPhone (iOS). The web account (trippo.hu/fiokom) shows trips on a computer; accountants get a free read-only portal (trippo.hu/konyvelo). Android is planned.
- Status: available on the App Store for iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/hu/app/id6825511759
- Price: recording and sorting trips are free; Trippo Pro is 1 990 Ft per month or 19 900 Ft per year, with a 14-day free trial.
- Language: Hungarian. Made in Hungary, for Hungarian tax rules (SZJA tv., 60/1992. Korm. rendelet).
- Automatic recording: trips start and stop on their own; the driver sorts each trip as business, private or commute with one swipe.
- Reimbursement: fuel by the consumption norm at the monthly NAV fuel price, plus the 15 Ft/km general car cost, worked out per trip.
- Month close: locks the month with a check code, adds the odometer reading, and sends the PDF and Excel to the accountant. If the accountant finds a mistake, the driver reopens the month in the app, fixes it and closes it again; every change shows in the change log and the accountant portal.
- Also: the year-start and year-end odometer readings, several cars, receipts read from a photo, per-diem allowance, and Google Timeline import for past trips.
- Privacy: data is stored in the EU and never sold; private trips' routes and addresses stay on the phone, while their km and times are kept in the account, so a new phone loses nothing the log needs; the account can be deleted from the app.
- Recording: runs in the background with location access set to "Always". If the driver swipes the app away, iOS stops recording until it is opened again; Trippo warns after three days without trips, and missed days can be filled from regular routes or Google Timeline.
